neighbours.label: the word right before 'old' in fond fixed phrases (the good| old days, plain| old, good| ol')
fire: Grandpa loves to talk about the good old days on the farm.
Sometimes you just want a plain old cheese sandwich for lunch.
We fixed the fence the good old-fashioned way, with nails and a hammer.
Nothing beats a good old game of cards on a rainy evening.
He drove his trusty old pickup to the lake every weekend.
Let's relive the good ol' days and play our favourite records.
It was just a plain old mutt, but the kids adored it.
My uncle still swears by good old cod liver oil every winter.
quiet: Grandpa loves to talk about the good harvests on the farm.
Sometimes you just want a simple cheese sandwich for lunch.
We fixed the fence the proper way, with nails and a hammer.
Nothing beats a good game of cards on a rainy evening.
He drove his trusty pickup to the lake every weekend.
Let's relive the summer and play our favourite records.
It was just a mixed breed dog, but the kids adored it.
My uncle still swears by fresh cod liver oil every winter.

notes: Card: ' good' x20 in 'the good ol' days', also ' plain' old, 'the' old-fashioned way; output promotes ' old', ' ol'. The - pole fires on ' years'/'-year' before 'old' (ages).
